title: Exactness of restriction of scalars
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring
$\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, a scheme $Y$, and an integer
$n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, and let $\widehat{\mathcal
O}_{E,Y}\twoheadrightarrow(A_{E,n})_Y$ be the reduction of the completed
coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Then the
restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_n$ is an exact functor

$$
 \operatorname{Res}_n:
 \Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})
 \longrightarrow\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)
$$

where the target means modules over $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, not over the discrete constant sheaf $(\mathcal O_E)_Y$, on the small pro-etale site
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

proof.text: Work on the small skeleton in the larger universe stipulated by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Abelian sheafification on this site is the functor of [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. Set $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ and $S=(A_{E,n})_Y$. The coefficient definition [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] supplies the projection $\pi_n:R\to S$ and identifies the two displayed module categories. By [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], restriction keeps the section groups, restriction maps and morphisms, with action $r m=\pi_n(r)m$. Thus it is additive, and forgetting its $R$-action gives exactly the same abelian sheaf as forgetting the original $S$-action.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian (forgetting module structure preserves kernels and cokernels)

proof.text: For both completed and finite quotient coefficient sheaves, the forgetful functor to abelian sheaves preserves finite limits and finite colimits by the module-sheaf forgetful theorem. After restriction of scalars, forgetting is definitionally the original forgetful functor on the finite quotient module category. Hence the composite of restriction with the completed-coefficient forgetful functor preserves finite limits and finite colimits.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian (forgetting module structure preserves kernels and cokernels)

proof.text: The forgetful functor from completed-coefficient module sheaves reflects finite limits and finite colimits: kernels and cokernels have the underlying abelian sheaf constructions, and the functor is faithful. Apply Mathlib.preservesFiniteLimits_of_reflects_of_preserves and preservesFiniteColimits_of_reflects_of_preserves to the composites in Step 2. Thus restriction itself preserves finite limits and finite colimits, which is the exactness assertion. This argument uses sheafified cokernels, not sectionwise surjectivity, and requires no flatness.
